::: {.why}
The continuous version connects sizing directly to the estimator whose standard error you spent week 7 on, which means the uncertainty in your Sharpe is uncertainty in your position size.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive the continuous-time Kelly leverage and express it in terms of the Sharpe ratio.
- Propagate the standard error of your Sharpe estimate into an interval on the optimal leverage, and state its width.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Derive the continuous version by maximising the growth rate, which is the mean times leverage minus half the variance times leverage squared. The optimum is the mean over the variance, which equals the Sharpe ratio divided by the volatility. Do the algebra and check it reduces to the discrete answer for small bets.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Propagate the uncertainty, which is the part that changes behaviour: with your pairs strategy's Sharpe and its standard error from qlib/stats.py, compute the implied optimal leverage and its confidence interval. The interval will span a factor of several, which is the honest argument for fractional Kelly and is stronger than any argument about risk aversion.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write that argument into reports/milestone-04-risk-model.md in three sentences.
:::
:::
